Thanks for following up. Six months ago our hospital's discharge process averaged 4.2 hours from physician order to the patient leaving the floor. Everyone blamed transport. When we actually walked the process with a stopwatch, transport was 20 minutes of it. The rest was waiting: pharmacy reconciliation queued behind morning rounds, discharge paperwork printed at a nurses' station on another floor, and family pickup that nobody called until the order was signed. We changed three things. Pharmacy started reconciling likely discharges the evening before. We moved the printer. And the unit clerk now calls the family the moment the physician says 'probably tomorrow', not when the order lands. Average is now 2.1 hours.  So as you can imagine, it's all hands until that's done — check back with me in a couple of months?
